newsitem.title: ISRAEL: VocalTec in pact with Motorola for voice over Internet.
newsitem.headline: VocalTec in pact with Motorola for voice over Internet.

text.p: Israel's VocalTec Ltd. said Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Motorola Inc. to license and distribute software for transmitting voice communications over the Internet and other computer networks.
VocalTec, which develops the software, said it was too early to discuss the financial aspects of the accord.

Under the agreement, VocalTec will supply its Telephone Gateway Server software to Motorola as part of an integrated software/hardware package. Motorola will sell the product to corporate clients, VocalTec chief financial officer Yahal Zilka told Reuters.
Other VocalTec products, such as the Internet Phone, will also be included in the agreement, he added.
The non-exclusive agreement is with Motorola's new Internet Software Products divison.
"Motorola decided that voice over Internet is an important development and created a division for it. As such they are tying up with VocalTec as the software supplier," Zilka said.
He said VocalTec had other re-selling agreements but that the one with Motorola marked a breakthrough for the company because of the American company's focus on Fortune 500 customers.

VocalTec develops and markets software that allows for voice and multimedia communications over the Internet and corporate intranets, as well as systems to bridge the Internet with the public switched phone network.
VocalTec's stock rose $2 to $8.50 early on Nasdaq. Schaumburg, Ill.-based Motorola edged up 37.5 cents to $56.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
